title: KPI thresholds and rollback oracle
body:
Purpose:
A compact, operational-first sheet that codifies KPI thresholds, escalation and automatic rollback rules for product launches (hosted + dedicated). Designed to be machine-readable notes for oncall and product ops, but still human-friendly.

Scope:
- Applies to new feature rollouts and model switches on Hosted API and Dedicated clusters.
- Focus on first 72h post-internal-launch and first 14 days for public ramps.

Quick summary (one-line):
If any SLO-adjacent KPI trips into red for > 3 mins (or sustained amber for > 15 min) for the launch cohort, trigger canary-pause → investigate → rollback according to the mapped rollback oracle.

Owner matrix (primary contact followed by escalation):
- Product lead: Maya Patel (primary) — slack: @maya — pager: OPS-PL-1
- Infra/Serving: Ethan Garcia — slack: @ethan — pager: SRE-2
- Observability: Priya Nair — slack: @priya — pager: OBS-1
- Customer Success: Lina Huang (notify for customer-impacting anomalies)

Key KPIs tracked (what to watch + intent):
- P50 latency (ms) — intent: latency health for typical requests
- P95 latency (ms) — intent: tail latency; sensitive to batching/queueing
- Error rate (% of 4xx/5xx per-minute) — intent: correctness and infra failures
- Token throughput (tokens/sec / cluster) — intent: capacity and throttling
- API timeouts (count/min) — intent: upstream timeouts and JVM/GPU stalls
- Cost-per-1k-tokens (USD) — intent: early economic outliers for new model variants
- Quality regression signal (eval-set QA fail rate) — intent: prompt-level correctness drops

Thresholds and immediate actions (Launch cohort = traffic routed to new variant):
- Green: metrics within baseline ±10% of expected (proceed)
- Amber: metric deviates 10–30% or P95 latency increases > 2x baseline for > 5 min → open incident channel + reduce traffic by 30% (manual/gating)
- Red: metric deviates >30% OR error rate > 1% sustained > 3 min OR API timeouts spike > 5x baseline for > 3 min → auto-canary-pause (traffic to new variant dropped to 0%), page oncall, trigger rollback playbook

Rollback oracle (ordered decision steps):
1) Auto-canary-pause: switch routing policy to fallback (previous stable model variant or lower-capacity plan) — executed by deployment pipeline step: rollouts/controller/abortWithFallback
2) Short-term mitigation (if canary pause successful): run degraded mode (limit max tokens per request, enforce smaller batch windows), notify docs & customers
3) Full rollback: if root cause appears to be model/regression or GPU OOM — revert to pinned version and restart serving nodes with validated kernel set
4) Post-rollback: run smoke eval (5 sample prompts from Eval set) and synthetic latency run (50 parallel clients x 5 sec each) before re-trying

Escalation ladder (timing + who to page):
- t = 0–10 min amber: Product lead + Obs engineer; Slack incident channel 
- t = 10–30 min amber or 3 min red: Page infra SRE and product ops commander
- t = 30+ min unresolved: Exec on-call (CTO), Legal (if customer-facing SLA risk)

Operational runbook (short checklist for oncall):
- Step 0: Confirm cohort identity and exact routing fraction (console -> rollout -> cohort details)
- Step 1: Check P95 latency, error-rate graphs (last 15m, 1h), and node-level OOM logs
- Step 2: If amber: reduce traffic to 30%, mark experiments/problem areas in tracking sheet
- Step 3: If red: trigger auto-canary-pause, record timestamp, open incident triage doc, notify CS
- Step 4: Collect artifacts: sample request/response payloads (scrub PII), GPU logs, kernel/driver versions
- Step 5: Decide: mitigations vs full rollback (use rollback oracle) and execute
- Step 6: Run post-action smoke tests and confirm stability for 30m before gradual re-open

Monitoring queries / alert pointers (examples to paste into Grafana/Prometheus):
- error_rate_per_min: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..|4..", route=~"/v1/generate"}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route=~"/v1/generate"}[1m]))
- p95_latency_ms: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) * 1000
- tokens_per_sec: sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m]))

Readiness scorecard (simple weighted score, target >= 85 to go >50% traffic):
- Infra health (35%): node error-rate, OOMs, kernel mismatches
- Latency (25%): P95 relative to baseline
- Quality (20%): Eval-set fail rate
- Cost (10%): projected cost-per-1k tokens compared to forecast
- Observability (10%): dashboards and alerts instrumented for the rollout
Scoring notes: each line scored 0–100, weighted average. Quick script in console can compute on demand.

Planned experiments / gating knobs (what we can toggle fast):
- Traffic fraction (% of new variant)
- Batch window (ms ceiling)
- Max tokens per request
- Quantization profile (q4_0 vs q8)
- Fallback model variant (smaller model / cheaper quantized variant)

Cost backstop rules (prevent runaway costs during live test):
- If cost-per-1k-tokens exceeds 3x forecast for > 30 min, auto-throttle to <10% traffic and notify finance-owner
- If projected hourly cost > $X (placeholder) mark emergency throttle and page billing owner

Notes to self (unfinished / TODOs):
- Hook in the new rollout API to emit "cohort_id" in traces (PR open: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-api#188)
- Add synthetic quality probes every 5m that run a quick eval-set through model variant
- Confirm whether dedicated clusters honor auto-canary-pause via routing policy (check infra runbook)
- Create template email for CS to tell customers in impacted cohort

Open questions for product review:
- What is acceptable short-term amber window for customer-facing SLAs (30 min vs 60 min)?
- Should cost-backstop be dollar-driven or ratio-driven for every customer tier?

Appendix: sample incident timeline (example):
- 2025-02-20 11:02 UTC — P95 spikes to 2.5x baseline (amber)
- 11:08 UTC — Amber persists; traffic reduced to 30% (manual)
- 11:11 UTC — Error rate rises to 1.8% (red) — auto-canary-pause triggers; page SRE
- 11:20 UTC — Root cause identified: kernel mismatch on 3 nodes; rollback to previous model variant initiated
- 11:35 UTC — Rollback complete; smoke eval run and green after 12m; slow reopen starting 12:00 UTC

Deliverables (what this doc should produce):
- A small automation patch that maps alert -> canary-pause (ops automation ticket assigned)
- A templated incident page (link to create) + CS/Legal notification templates
- A readiness webhook for rollout UI to display the weighted readiness score

References / useful links:
- internal rollout console: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts
- eval harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals
- incident template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Incident+Template

End of doc.
